correctness.rationale: Stationarity follows by solving \(q=pq+(1-q)p^2\). The exact inequalities \(p-h(p)=p(1-p)^2/D(p)\) and \(h(p)=1-(1-p)/D(p)\), with \(D(p)=(p-1/2)^2+3/4\), prove the universal upper bound and identify a supporting line at the nearest-to-half discrete composition. Strict convexity of h on \([0,1/2]\) and the explicit slope gap \((u-1)(2u-1)/D(u)^2\) show that the proposed lower polygon is convex. Jensen and two-point distributions give the sharp lower envelope for all \(g\ge2\), plus the parity contact sets. Exact arithmetic checks pass on 3318 lattice points, 4970 finite profiles and a four-edge reversal witness; the general proof does not depend on these tests.
risks: Finite lattice or random tests alone would not prove unbounded g; the proof is analytic.
Realizable composition distributions are topology-constrained when fixed connected overlaps are prescribed.

Earlier game-transition and variable-game papers optimize evolutionary selection, not the same stationary environment occupancy functional over g-uniform cooperator-count laws. evidence: Wei 2026 sections 3.1-3.2 explicitly analyze high-value state fractions and quality/scale of hyperedges.
RESULT.md gives the exact all-size sharp envelope and four-group witness.
value.rationale: The paper simulates both high-value group frequency and cooperator clustering, so the precise uncertainty in environmental quality at a fixed total cooperator budget is a motivated mathematical gap. The theorem completely solves its sharp upper and lower distributional bounds for every integer hyperedge size, with a surprising switch in lower-bound extremizers near half-occupancy and an exact odd/even contact classification. A single four-group example shows that reshuffling cooperation at unchanged total cooperation can move abundance above or below the uniform-composition baseline. This is a natural exact classification, not merely an arbitrary computed slice. The theorem deliberately does not claim a global coevolutionary prediction.
risks: The mathematical impact is bounded by the frozen-strategy assumption and specific sensitivity exponents.
For fixed connected hypergraph topology, accessible compositions may be a strict subset of the distributional feasible set.
